card.name: Closing points before a restriction or instruction
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a linking word that ends a condition clause, such as a closing bracket after Child-Pugh class C or the comma after "If particulate matter is observed". It also fires on words like "not" or "recommended" in negative statements about use.

modes.label: Closing bracket after severity class
modes.description: The closing parenthesis after a hepatic impairment grade, just before a bracketed cross-reference or a statement about avoiding use.
modes.example: Avoid the use of IMBRUVICA in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C<<)>> [see Use in Specific Populations (

modes.label: Comma after a visual-inspection condition
modes.description: The comma that ends an "if particulate matter is observed" clause, right before an instruction not to use the product.
modes.example: If particulate matter is observed<<,>> do not administer.

modes.label: Negated use or limits
modes.description: Words inside statements that something is not recommended, not studied, or contraindicated below a threshold.
modes.example: The use of REYATAZ in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) is not<< recommended>>.

card.writes: It seems to steer the model away from warning words, toward a plain continuation such as a negation or a direct instruction.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a condition has just been stated and a restriction or "do not use" is about to follow.
